question: Describe all the specific tools and programmes used under Project Elephant for welfare, human-elephant conflict mitigation, and habitat policy — Gaja Suchana, Project RE-HAB, Gajraj, and RAPs.
cardAnswer: For domesticated elephant welfare: the Gaja Suchana App is used for mandatory DNA profiling of all captive elephants to prevent illegal trade and monitor welfare. For human-elephant conflict (HEC): Project RE-HAB (Reducing Elephant-Human Attacks using Bees) uses bee fences to deter elephants from human settlements. The Gajraj system is an AI-based intrusion detection system installed by Indian Railways to prevent elephant-train collisions on critical railway stretches. For habitat policy: Regional Action Plans (RAPs) represent a shift from state-specific to regional frameworks to account for transboundary elephant movement.

question: Describe the MIKE Programme completely — full name, initiation, authority, sub-regional office, all 10 Indian sites, and all three objectives including the PIKE Index.
cardAnswer: MIKE stands for Monitoring of Illegal Killings of Elephants. It was initiated in South Asia in 2003 as a result of a COP resolution of CITES — not IUCN or WWF. The Sub-Regional Support Office for South Asia is in New Delhi (supported by IUCN South Asia). There are 10 official MIKE sites in India: Chirang-Ripu, Dihing Patkai, Deomali, Garo Hills, Eastern Dooars, Mayurbhanj, Shivalik, Mysore, Nilgiri, and Wayanad. Note: there are 33 Elephant Reserves but only 10 MIKE sites — the numbers differ significantly. The three objectives are: (1) Measure levels and trends in illegal elephant hunting; (2) Identify causes of changes in those trends; (3) Evaluate the impact of CITES decisions on illegal killing trends. MIKE calculates the PIKE Index (Proportion of Illegally Killed Elephants) to monitor poaching pressure.

question: Describe the Haathi Mere Saathi programme and E-8 Ministerial Meeting completely — launch partners, 2025 status, focus tagline, mascot, awards, E-8 date, countries, significance, and the E-50:50 trap.
cardAnswer: Haathi Mere Saathi was launched by MoEFCC and WTI (Wildlife Trust of India) — NOT WWF-India. By 2025, it became a nationwide awareness campaign involving 1.2 million students, with the launch of Gaj Gaurav Awards for frontline forest heroes. Its focus is 'Taking Gajah to Prajah' using AI, remote sensing, and community engagement. The mascot is Gaju. The E-8 Ministerial Meeting was initiated on 24th May 2011 in Delhi, involving 8 countries: India, Botswana, Republic of Congo, Indonesia, Kenya, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, and Thailand. Its significance was bringing together range countries covering all three elephant species — Asian Elephant, African Bush Elephant, and African Forest Elephant. The E-50:50 Forum was originally proposed as an international congress for 50 countries to adopt a 50-year vision, but it never materialised as planned; its goals are now addressed via World Elephant Day summits and Project Elephant Steering Committees.
